role_sought: Member of the Slovak National Council, Party of the Democratic Left (SDĽ) list
detail: Elections held on 5–6 June 1992. First election to parliament; the SDĽ came second behind Vladimír Mečiar's HZDS (37.26%). The Slovak National Council became the National Council of the Slovak Republic on independence in 1993.

role_sought: Member of the National Council, Spoločná voľba (Common Choice) list, an SDĽ-led coalition
detail: Elections held on 30 September–1 October 1994. The Statistical Office's list of elected deputies includes Robert Fico for SP.VOĽBA; the coalition's vote share is published only as an image on the official site, so it is not reproduced here.

role_sought: Member of the National Council, SDĽ list (3rd on the list)
vote_share: SDĽ: 492,507 votes (14.66%); Fico: 194,519 preferential votes (39.50% of SDĽ voters), moving from 3rd to 1st place on the list
detail: Elections held on 25–26 September 1998. He received the most preferential votes of any SDĽ candidate; the SDĽ joined Mikuláš Dzurinda's coalition, which Fico later criticised before leaving the party in 1999.

role_sought: Member of the National Council; leader of Smer
detail: Elections held on 20–21 September 2002, the first contested by Smer. Mikuláš Dzurinda formed a second centre-right government.

role_sought: Member of the National Council; Smer-SD leader and candidate for Prime Minister
detail: Fico formed a coalition with the SNS and ĽS-HZDS. The Statistical Office's 2006 results pages are no longer reachable on volby.statistics.sk; figures from The Slovak Spectator's report of the final results.

role_sought: Member of the National Council; Smer-SD leader and candidate for Prime Minister
result: Won (first place) but no majority; elected MP, went into opposition
detail: His coalition partners lost ground (ĽS-HZDS fell below the threshold) and the four centre-right parties formed a government under Iveta Radičová.

role_sought: Member of the National Council; Smer-SD leader and candidate for Prime Minister
detail: Early election after the fall of the Radičová government in October 2011; Smer-SD became the first single party to win an absolute majority since 1993.

role_sought: President of the Slovak Republic (Smer-SD candidate)
result: First place; advanced to the run-off
opponent: Andrej Kiska 455,996 (24.00%); Radoslav Procházka 403,548 (21.24%); Milan Kňažko 244,401 (12.86%)
detail: Turnout 43.40%. Fico announced his candidacy on 18 December 2013 while serving as Prime Minister.

role_sought: President of the Slovak Republic (Smer-SD candidate)
detail: After the defeat he remained Prime Minister.

role_sought: Member of the National Council; Smer-SD leader and candidate for Prime Minister
detail: President Andrej Kiska asked Fico to form a government on 9 March 2016; he formed a coalition with the SNS, Most-Híd and #Sieť. The official results site renders its tables with scripts; vote totals cross-checked with TASR and Wikipedia.

role_sought: Member of the National Council; Smer-SD chairman (the list was led by Prime Minister Peter Pellegrini)
opponent: OĽaNO–NOVA–KÚ–ZZ (Igor Matovič), 721,166 votes (25.03% per Wikipedia), 53 seats
detail: Igor Matovič formed the new government. Pellegrini, who had received more preferential votes than Fico, left Smer-SD in June 2020 and founded Hlas-SD. The official results site renders its tables with scripts; figures from Wikipedia.

role_sought: Member of the National Council; Smer-SD leader and candidate for Prime Minister
detail: Early election after the fall of the Heger government. Fico formed a coalition with Hlas-SD and the SNS, appointed on 25 October 2023. The Statistical Office publishes percentages to two decimals without rounding (22.94%); some sources round to 22.95%. The official tables render with scripts; figures cross-checked with Wikipedia.
